Soojin — Draft attached. High level points included in "attacker-lateralization-lattice.pdf":

- Principle: explicit demarcation of control-plane (management APIs, model registry, orchestrator) and data-plane (inference runtime, KV cache, batching queues). Default deployments use separate VPC subnets with strict SGs and no inbound control-plane access from inference subnets.

- Sidecar failure modes considered: transient process crash, OOM-induced restart, network partition, misconfiguration leading to degraded KV cache. For each we show: detection (liveness/probe and tracing), containment (sidecar soft-handoff + reject-to-fallback model), recovery (replay-safe checkpointing), and forensics (request-id correlated logs).

- Lateralization mitigations: least-privilege service accounts per-tenant; per-tenant encryption keys (KMS envelope) for persisted KV entries; ephemeral local cache with TTL and automatic invalidation on redeploy; egress gateway allowlist per-tenant; strict mTLS with per-pod certs and short TTLs for in-cluster connections; and network policy deny-by-default with explicit exceptions.

- Operational playbook excerpt: automatic model-fallback to smaller quantized variant on cache failure; circuit-breaker on tokenization or batching anomalies to avoid cache poisoning; rapid rollback via pinned-version routing.

Attachments included (stubs):
 - attacker-lateralization-lattice.pdf (2 pages — lattice + mitigations)
 - sidecar-failure-modes.pdf (3 pages — detection/containment/recovery flows)
 - network-demarcation-diagram.png (SVG exported as PNG)

Alice — attaching the concise artifacts you requested and summarizing the key points below. We kept items short so your auditors can thumb through quickly.

Attachments (stubs):
- network-demarcation-diagram.png (image/png, 460KB) — shows VPC subnets for control-plane vs inference-data-plane, egress gateway placement, and per-tenant routing fences.
- sidecar-failure-modes.pdf (application/pdf, 180KB) — triage matrix for process crash, OOM/restart loops, network partition, and config drift; includes detection hooks and recommended alert thresholds.
- attacker-lateralization-lattice.pdf (application/pdf, 120KB) — two-page lattice mapping attacker goals to mitigations and evidence types (logs, mTLS cert rotation, KMS audit).
- evidence-log-snippet.txt (text/plain, 6KB) — sanitized sample trace showing control-plane request id -> sidecar ack -> egress deny event.

Concise answers:
1) Network demarcation: We enforce explicit subnet isolation (control-plane in a distinct management VPC, inference runtime in tenant-scoped VPCs or subnets). Only control-plane egress to management endpoints is allowed via strongly audited egress gateways. All inter-subnet traffic is governed by network policies and security groups; default posture is deny-all.

2) Sidecar failure handling: Sidecars expose liveness/readiness; on liveness failure we trigger: (a) immediate divert to fallback model variant, (b) request requeue with dedup token to avoid double-processing, (c) spawn-of-last-known-good sidecar replica in a warmed pool where configured. KV cache corruption protection uses write-ahead checksums and tombstone markers; on detection we flush to read-through mode backed by persistent store.

3) Lateralization / lateral movement: Prevented via per-tenant identity and network fences, per-tenant KMS keys, mTLS with short TTLs, and egress allowlists. We also run periodic simulated lateralization tests as part of our penetration cadence and provide attestations (signed reports) upon customer request.

Next steps: if you'd like we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough with diagrams on Mon. Link to artifacts (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1a2b3c-sidecar-packets

If you need any additional evidence artifacts (audit-config exports or cert rotation logs) we can provide an auditor packet under an NDA.
